skill.name: python-style-guide
skill.description: Comprehensive Python style guidance based on Google's Python Style Guide. Use it to write, review, and refactor Python code with consistent imports, type annotations, docstrings, naming, formatting, and maintainability rules.
skill.summary: Apply Google-style Python rules to write and review clean, typed, maintainable code.
skill.author: CodingKaiser

security_audit.summary: All reviewed static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, prose, license text, or reference links. The skill is a Python style guide and I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable scripts, or unsafe tool behavior in the cited files.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger command and eval detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dangerous examples clearly labeled as anti-patterns and prefer non-executable reference examples where possible.

remediation.issue: Reference links and sample URLs trigger network detectors.
remediation.suggestion: Use example.com for samples and make clear that links are documentation references, not skill actions.

static_findings.snippet: authority to forbid You from making technical modifications
result = eval(user_input)  # WRONG - major security risk
ValueError: If user_id is invalid or data is empty.
username: The invalid username that caused the error.
Use `import` statements for packages and modules only, not for individual classes or functions.
- One import per line (except for multiple items from `typing` or `collections.abc`)
Use exceptions appropriately. Do not suppress errors with bare `except:` clauses.
- Use built-in types (`list`, `dict`, `set`) instead of `typing.List`, etc. (Python 3.9+)
- Import typing symbols directly: `from typing import Any, Union`
Use implicit false where possible. Empty sequences, `None`, and `0` are false in boolean contexts.
- Single character names except for counters/iterators (`i`, `j`, `k`)
Use `%` formatting for logging, not f-strings (allows lazy evaluation):
Always use context managers (`with` statements) for file operations:
Run `pylint` on all Python code. Suppress warnings only when necessary with clear explanations:
Comprehensive guidelines for writing clean, maintainable Python code based on [Google's Python Style
x = "name: " + name + "; score: " + str(score)  # Avoid + for formatting
Generally avoid multiple statements on one line.

content.value_statement: Python teams need consistent code style, type hints, and review guidance. This skill applies Google-style Python rules for cleaner imports, docstrings, formatting, and maintainable code.
actual_capabilities: Guides import organization, absolute imports, and direct typing imports.
Explains exception handling, boolean checks, comprehensions, lambdas, and default arguments.
Defines naming, formatting, line length, indentation, comments, and docstring conventions.
Provides examples for Google-style function, class, module, and async docstrings.
Covers advanced typing patterns, including Protocol, TypedDict, Literal, TypeAlias, and ParamSpec.
Identifies common Python anti-patterns and suggests safer or cleaner alternatives.
limitations: It gives style guidance but does not run a formatter, linter, or test suite.
Some rules may conflict with an existing project style and need local adaptation.
It focuses on Python style, not full application architecture or runtime performance.
Security examples are educational and do not replace a dedicated security review.

use_cases.title: Review Python Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check imports, names, docstrings, annotations, and common anti-patterns before merging Python changes.

use_cases.title: Refactor Existing Modules
use_cases.description: Apply consistent style rules while improving readability, type clarity, and resource handling in older code.

use_cases.title: Teach Team Standards
use_cases.description: Create shared Python guidance for contributors who need clear examples and review expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a short Python snippet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python code against the Python style guide. Focus on naming, imports, formatting, and simple readability issues.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Docstrings
prompt_templates.scenario: Add or revise documentation for public APIs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite the docstrings in this Python module using Google-style docstrings. Preserve behavior and mention any missing type information.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor for Type Clarity
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate refactor with annotations and cleaner structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Python code to follow the guide. Improve type annotations, imports, exception handling, and function size without changing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Python Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across style, typing, and anti-patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Python module using the full style guide. Prioritize issues by impact and provide a concise remediation plan.

output_examples.input: A Python function with mixed imports, missing annotations, and unclear names.
output: Imports are regrouped by standard library, third-party, and local modules.
Function parameters and return value receive explicit type annotations.
Ambiguous names are replaced with descriptive lower_with_under names.

output_examples.input: A public class with minimal documentation.
output: The class receives a concise Google-style summary.
Attributes and constructor arguments are documented in separate sections.
Raised exceptions are listed only when they are part of the public contract.

output_examples.input: A module containing mutable defaults, broad exceptions, and complex comprehensions.
output: Mutable defaults are replaced with a None sentinel pattern.
Broad exception handling is narrowed to specific exception types.
Complex comprehensions are converted into readable loops.

best_practices: Ask for style review after sharing enough surrounding code to preserve local conventions.
Request prioritized findings when reviewing large modules or pull requests.
Pair this guide with project linters and tests before accepting refactors.
anti_patterns: Do not apply every rule mechanically when the existing project clearly uses another standard.
Do not request behavior changes when the goal is only style cleanup.
Do not use the examples as production code without adapting names, errors, and validation.

faq.question: What style guide does this skill use?
faq.answer: It is based on Google's Python Style Guide and adds examples for common review tasks.

faq.question: Can it format code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review comments, but it does not run formatting tools.

faq.question: Does it support type annotation reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers function annotations, built-in collection types, TypeAlias, Protocol, TypedDict, and related patterns.

faq.question: Can it write Google-style docstrings?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for modules, functions, classes, exceptions, properties, and async functions.

faq.question: Should it override my project style?
faq.answer: No. The guide says to match surrounding code when a project already has clear conventions.

faq.question: Is this a security scanning skill?
faq.answer: No. It mentions safer Python patterns, but it is mainly a style and maintainability guide.
